system.name: TLT
system.one_liner: a system that accelerates reasoning RL training losslessly via adaptive speculative decoding

components.name: Target Model
components.role: the large model that generates one token per step in vanilla decoding, and verifies all drafted tokens in parallel in speculative decoding

components.name: Draft Model
components.role: lightweight model that rapidly generates a sequence of candidate tokens for verification

components.name: Drafting Stage
components.role: draft model proposes a run of candidate tokens (numbered steps)

components.name: Verification Stage
components.role: target model verifies the drafted tokens in a single parallel forward pass, accepting up to the first mismatch

components.name: Roofline Model Analysis
components.role: H100 tensor TFLOPS vs. batch size plot showing speculative decoding reaches peak throughput at a much smaller batch size than vanilla decoding

flows.what: vanilla decoding generates one new token per step, feeding it back as input for the next step
drafted token sequence sent for parallel verification
accepts drafted tokens up to the first mismatch, keeps target's own token at that position

content.key_idea: Speculative decoding replaces vanilla decoding's one-token-per-step loop with a draft model proposing several tokens at once and the target model verifying them all in a single parallel pass, which the roofline analysis shows reaches peak GPU throughput at far smaller batch sizes.
content.reading_order: Left column top-to-bottom: (a) vanilla decoding example above (c) roofline chart; right column: (b) speculative decoding's drafting stage above its verification stage.

evidence: a lightweight draft model rapidly generates a sequence of candidate tokens ... verified in parallel by the much larger target model
The system accepts the drafted sequence up to the first token that mismatches the target model's prediction
this process improves throughput by shifting the typically memory-bound autoregressive generation towards a more compute-bound operation

summary: This figure explains speculative decoding as background for TLT. Panel (a) shows vanilla decoding: the target model generates one new token per step, sequentially extending the sequence. Panel (b) shows speculative decoding in two stages: a Drafting Stage where a lightweight draft model proposes several candidate tokens at once, and a Verification Stage where the target model checks all of them in a single parallel pass, keeping accepted tokens (green) up to the first rejected one (red) and substituting its own token there. Panel (c) is a roofline-style plot of H100 tensor TFLOPS versus batch size, showing that speculative decoding (yellow line) reaches peak compute throughput at a much smaller batch size than vanilla decoding (red line), illustrated with a gray arrow. A shared legend defines prompt/drafted/accepted/rejected token colors used across panels (a) and (b).
summary_zh: 该图介绍推测解码背景：(a)传统解码逐token生成；(b)推测解码分起草阶段（草稿模型批量生成候选token）与验证阶段（目标模型并行验证，接受绿色token、拒绝红色token）；(c)屋顶线分析显示推测解码在更小批大小即可达到峰值吞吐。
